<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 4:18">Ib.</cite> ed. Lag. <he>נוֹהֲרֵיה</he> (oth. ed. <he>נַהֲרֵי</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 18:29">Targ. Ps. XVIII, 29</cite> (ed. Lag. <he>ניהור</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 6:23">Targ. Prov. VI, 23</cite> <he>נוֹהֲ׳</he>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Genesis 1:5">Gen. I, 5</cite>) <he>קרייה רחמנא לנ׳ וכ׳</he> the Lord called the light and appointed it over the service of the day. Ib. 7ᵇ <he>נ׳ דאבוקה</he> torch-light; <he>נ׳ דשרגא</he> candle-light; <he>דנפיש נ׳ טובא</he> whose light is very strong; <he>דזוטר נ׳ טפי</he> whose light is very small (of limited range). Ib. 8ᵃ; <cite ref="Horayot 12a:10">Hor. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>משיך נְהוֹרֵיה</he>, v. <cite ref="M02892"><he>מְשַׁךְ</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <cite ref="T00152"><he>רבתי</he></cite> (<he>חד כות׳</he> 1) <he>זיתא נ׳ וכ׳</he> the olive tree (in thy dream) means light &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 52b:29">Ber. 52ᵇ</cite> <he>חדא נ׳ איכא בנורא</he> fire contains only one sort of light.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 83b:22">B. Kam. 83ᵇ</cite> <he>דילמא נ׳ שקיל מיניה וכ׳</he> perhaps the law says (<cite ref="Exodus 21:24">Ex. XXI, 24</cite>), he deprived him of his eye-sight, let him be deprived of his eye-sight?—
Kidd. 24ᵇ נ׳ בריא good (normal) eye-sight, נ׳ כחישא defective sight; a. fr.—[Y. Orl. II, 62ᶜ top נהור אתית, v. נְהַר I.]—סגי נ׳ rich of light, euphem. for blind.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 8:8:13">Y. Peah VIII, end, 21ᵇ</cite>, v. infra; a. e.—Pl. <cite ref="N00865"><he>נְהוֹרִין</he></cite>, <he>נְהוֹרַיָּא</he>, <cite ref="N00864"><he>נְהוֹרֵי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 1:14">Targ. Gen. I, 14</cite>; <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 1:16">16</cite>; a. fr.—Ber. l. c. <he>טובא נ׳ איכא בנורא</he> there is a combination of lights in fire, v. <cite ref="M00015"><he>מָאוֹר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 21:1">Pesik. R. s. 21</cite> <he>הא ברייתי לך תרין נְהוֹרִים וכ׳</he> I created two lights for thee, thy father and thy mother; a. fr.—<he>סגי</he>(<cite ref="A00000"><he>א</he></cite>) <he>נהוריא</he>, v. supra.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 5:5:4">Y. Peah V, end, 19ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 23:10">Prov. XXIII, 10</cite>, quot. in Mish.

<cite ref="Proverbs 5:6">ib. V, 6</cite> <cite ref="P00255"><he>עוֹלִים</he></cite>, Ms. M. a. Y. ed. <he>עולם</he>) <he>אלו שירדו מנכסיהן … סַגַּיָּא נ׳</he> by ‘those going up’ are meant those who went down from their estates (reduced to poverty), as the blind are euphemistically called rich of light. Y. Keth. I, 25ᵃ bot. [read:] <he>כאינשי דצווחין לסמייה סגיא נ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 8:8:13">Y. Peah VIII, end, 21ᵇ</cite> <he>חד דס׳ נ׳</he> one of the blind men (whom the charitable honored by inviting them to their tables).
